topic: Sunday deep dive: everything Joy Boy left behind during the Void Century, chronologically, from the Great War through the Ancient Weapons, the Poneglyphs, the empty throne, Laugh Tale, and his eventual return
title: The Void Century: Everything Joy Boy Left Behind
description:
The Void Century is the one hundred years the World Government erased from every record on the planet, and researching it is the single worst crime in this world. This deep dive walks through everything Joy Boy actually left behind during that century, in order: the Great War, the three Ancient Weapons, the thirty Poneglyphs, the throne that was never really empty, a broken promise to an entire ocean kingdom, and the island where it all ends in laughter.

Every major mystery this franchise has ever teased, Imu, the Will of D, the Ancient Weapons, the One Piece itself, traces back to this one century. This is the full shape of it, with the exact chapters that prove each piece.
comment: Is Imu really the final villain of this story, or is there someone above him? Pick one.

lines.text: Because the first piece of this isn't a treasure or a weapon. It's a war nobody alive remembers fighting...

lines.text: Nine hundred years ago, twenty kingdoms went to war against something they called the Great Kingdom.

lines.text: That alliance of twenty royal families would eventually become the World Government you see today.

lines.text: Every island you've ever seen in this story is just the mountaintop of a continent that used to stand taller.

shot.fallback: golden ruined city sinking beneath clouds

shot.fallback: scientist pointing to a hidden ancient weapon

lines.text: Which means, by his own math, this war never actually finished nine hundred years ago. It just paused.

lines.text: The Great Kingdom itself had a real name, one Professor Clover said held the entire key to understanding this century.

lines.text: Nobody alive has ever said that name out loud on the page. Not once.

shot.fallback: blank space on an ancient carved stone

lines.text: According to Vegapunk, the Great Kingdom was five hundred years ahead of where the world is now, technologically.

shot.fallback: ancient advanced machinery buried in ruins

shot.fallback: scientist humbled before ancient technology

shot.fallback: twenty royal crests representing ancient kingdoms

shot.fallback: giants examining an ancient carved mural skeptically

lines.text: That mural lines up almost exactly with an ancient text called the Harley, which describes two worlds already gone and one still coming.

shot.fallback: ancient prophetic text glowing with faint light

lines.text: Before the war, an entire tribe called the Shandorians lived on the moon, alongside a race of ancient robots.

shot.fallback: ancient tribe standing beside towering robots on the moon

lines.text: When resources up there ran out, three different races traveled down together to this planet.

shot.search: three races travel moon to planet
shot.fallback: ancient travelers descending from the moon together

lines.text: The Shandorians ended up on the island of Jaya, where they built their own city: Shandora.

shot.fallback: golden city rising on a lush island

lines.text: Shandora collapses during this same war, defended by people fighting something the records only call those who seek the stone.

shot.fallback: ancient city crumbling under siege

shot.fallback: descendants guarding ancient ruined golden city

lines.text: On Dressrosa, the Tontatta dwarves were already being oppressed by the Donquixote family even before the Void Century started.

shot.fallback: small dwarf tribe suffering under a cruel ruling family

lines.text: By the present day, even the dwarves themselves have completely forgotten what actually happened back then.

shot.fallback: small dwarf village with no memory of its own past

lines.text: There's a reason the World Nobles live at the very top of the Red Line, the tallest point in the entire world.

lines.text: If sea levels rose two hundred meters once already, rising further is apparently not a risk they're willing to take at ground level.

lines.text: That same fear is why they commission four massive structures: Tequila Wolf, Vodka Wolf, Rum Wolf, and Bourbon Wolf.

shot.fallback: four colossal wolf-shaped structures under construction

lines.text: Slaves have reportedly been constructing those four megastructures for seven hundred straight years.

shot.fallback: laborers constructing a massive structure for generations

lines.text: Nobody low enough in this world's hierarchy gets told why those structures actually matter.

shot.fallback: workers kept in the dark about their own labor

lines.text: Every decision the World Government makes about geography traces back to a disaster they caused themselves, nine centuries ago.

shot.fallback: world map reshaped by an ancient catastrophe

lines.text: The alliance that wins this war doesn't even get to enjoy a clean victory. They spend the next eight centuries just trying to keep the secret buried.

shot.fallback: ancient council guarding a buried secret for generations

lines.text: That's the actual cost of winning: an entire government built around hiding exactly how it started.

shot.fallback: government headquarters built atop a hidden truth

shot.fallback: robed elders rushing to silence a live broadcast

lines.text: They only partly succeed. Enough of the truth gets out that it can never be fully buried again.

shot.fallback: fragments of a broadcast still spreading despite interference

lines.text: Joy Boy's side loses in the end. The alliance wins, and the Void Century quietly begins...

lines.text: He becomes close with Zunesha during this life, a friendship that still matters eight centuries later.

shot.fallback: massive robot powering down mid-climb

shot.search: Emet iron giant more than machine

lines.text: An ancient weapon built right as this century began ends up being the thing that saves Joy Boy's return eight hundred years later.

shot.fallback: ancient robot standing guard over a historic return

lines.text: Nobody has explained yet why an iron giant built at the start of this century would end up protecting Joy Boy's return at the very end of it.

lines.text: That's the kind of century this was: even the machines built during it are still deciding outcomes today...

shot.fallback: ancient robot silhouetted against a modern battlefield

lines.text: Here's the part most retellings rush past: the Ancient Weapons aren't just big and scary. Each one is completely different.

shot.fallback: three distinct ancient weapons displayed side by side

lines.text: Pluton is a battleship, built on Water 7 during the Void Century, capable of leveling entire nations.

shot.fallback: massive ancient battleship under construction at a shipyard

lines.text: Its blueprints survive for centuries, passed shipwright to shipwright, until they land with a fish-man named Tom.

shot.fallback: old shipwright guarding ancient battleship blueprints

lines.text: Tom refuses to hand them over to the government, no matter what they threaten him with.

shot.fallback: shipwright standing firm against government agents

lines.text: His apprentice Franky eventually burns those blueprints completely rather than risk them ending up in the wrong hands.

shot.fallback: cyborg shipwright burning ancient blueprints in flames

lines.text: Pluton itself is hidden inside Wano, buried under a mountain the country built walls specifically to flood and seal away.

shot.fallback: ancient battleship buried beneath a flooded mountain

lines.text: Opening Wano's borders was never really about tourism. It was always about bringing down that one wall.

shot.fallback: towering wall surrounding an isolated ancient country

lines.text: Wano wasn't always shaped like a water bowl. Before the Void Century, it was just a normal island at sea level.

shot.search: ancient Wano normal island sea level
shot.fallback: flat ordinary island before it was transformed

lines.text: Oden learns on his trip to Laugh Tale that Wano adopted its isolation specifically to protect itself from something it only ever calls a great enemy.

shot.search: Oden learns Wano isolation great enemy
shot.fallback: samurai discovering why his country sealed itself away

lines.text: That's why the walls went up in the first place, flooding everything below the top of them and leaving only a few mountainside plateaus to live on.

shot.fallback: towering walls flooding a once-open country

lines.text: Even the people living inside Wano today have no idea why their own country is isolated at all.

shot.fallback: villagers living unaware of their country's hidden history

lines.text: Poseidon isn't a machine at all. It's a person: a mermaid princess born once every few centuries with the power to command Sea Kings.

shot.search: Poseidon mermaid princess Sea Kings power
shot.fallback: mermaid princess commanding giant Sea Kings

lines.text: During the Void Century, that power belonged to a different princess entirely. Today, it belongs to Shirahoshi.

shot.fallback: mermaid princess inheriting an ancient power

lines.text: Even the Sea Kings themselves don't fully understand why their ruler keeps being born this exact way.

shot.fallback: giant sea creatures bowing to a mysterious ruler

lines.text: And then there's Uranus, the third weapon, which the story has never actually shown you anything about.

shot.fallback: empty fog where a third ancient weapon should be

lines.text: Not its shape. Not its location. Not even a hint of what it actually does.

shot.fallback: blank unmarked space representing total mystery

lines.text: Three weapons, one war, and only one of them is still a total mystery nine hundred years later...

shot.fallback: three ancient relics, one still hidden in fog

lines.text: All three weapons share one detail that's easy to miss: they're named after actual gods, for exactly the kind of power they hold.

shot.fallback: three weapons glowing with godlike divine energy

lines.text: Pluton isn't the only one people chase without understanding what they're chasing. Crocodile builds an entire criminal organization just hunting for it.

shot.fallback: desert warlord commanding a criminal organization

lines.text: Spandam, a government agent, wants it too, officially to end the Pirate Era, actually to overthrow the same government he works for.

shot.fallback: government agent secretly plotting betrayal

lines.text: Poseidon pulls in obsession too. A pirate named Vander Decken spends years fixated on Shirahoshi without even fully understanding what she actually is.

shot.fallback: obsessive pirate fixated on a mermaid princess

lines.text: That's the real theme connecting all three weapons: they don't have to be understood to be wanted. They just have to be powerful.

shot.fallback: three weapons desired despite being misunderstood

lines.text: Franky himself never wanted that power in the first place. He built his entire life protecting the one person who could actually unlock it.

shot.fallback: cyborg shipwright protecting an archaeologist friend

lines.text: That's the quiet twist in all of this: the person most qualified to misuse Pluton is also the one person who's spent her whole life trying not to.

shot.fallback: archaeologist choosing restraint over ancient power

lines.text: The government never manages to get its hands on a working Pluton blueprint, specifically because of choices people like Tom and Franky kept making.

shot.fallback: government agents failing to seize ancient blueprints

lines.text: Three weapons, and the story's entire cast keeps choosing, over and over, not to use the two that are actually findable...

shot.fallback: heroes turning away from accessible ancient power

lines.text: The Poneglyphs are the only physical record left of any of this, and they're deliberately built to never break.

shot.fallback: massive indestructible stone tablet glowing faintly

lines.text: A clan of master stonemasons in Wano, the Kouzuki family, carved these things specifically so history couldn't be erased again.

shot.fallback: ancient stonemasons carving a massive stone tablet

lines.text: There are thirty of them scattered across the world: historical ones, instructional ones, and four rare road ones.

shot.fallback: scattered ancient stone tablets across a world map

lines.text: You can actually tell them apart just by color: historical and instructional stones are dark blue, road stones are a deep red.

shot.fallback: stones glowing in two distinct colors side by side

lines.text: The historical stones hold pieces of the Void Century itself. The instructional ones point toward where to find more.

shot.fallback: ancient tablet pointing toward another hidden stone

lines.text: The four road stones, read together, point to one single location: the last island on the Grand Line.

shot.fallback: four glowing red stones aligning toward one point

lines.text: There's also a single combined message called the Rio Poneglyph, built from nine of the historical stones put together.

shot.fallback: nine ancient stones merging into one message

lines.text: Finding it means carrying instructional passages with you across your entire voyage, piece by piece, the same way Roger apparently did.

shot.fallback: pirate carrying ancient passages across a long journey

lines.text: Reading any of them requires an ancient script almost nobody alive can translate.

shot.fallback: scholar squinting at unreadable ancient script

lines.text: Only a handful of people in the entire world can actually read it: Nico Robin, the Kouzuki family, and Vegapunk.

shot.fallback: three scholars studying the same ancient script

lines.text: Robin learned it by secretly spying on her own mother's research team at the age of eight.

shot.search: young Robin spies mother research team
